plain_english_policy: This bill (HB648) establishes a **strict environmental buffer zone** around the Chattahoochee River in Alabama by prohibiting new landfills and junkyards within one mile of its banks outside municipal boundaries. It does not apply to existing facilities or those on-site at industrial plants, nor does it address enforcement beyond injunctive relief (court orders). The policy direction is **protectionist**, aiming to reduce pollution risks from waste disposal near a major waterway by restricting new development in the vicinity.
policy_direction_if_enacted: If enacted, HB648 would create a **de facto environmental protection regime** for the Chattahoochee River. The policy direction aligns with **pollution prevention and watershed conservation**, prioritizing public health and water quality over industrial or commercial expansion near the river. It reflects a **proactive regulatory stance** by preempting future land-use conflicts that could harm the river’s ecosystem, though it does not mandate cleanup of existing violations or expand enforcement beyond court action.
sponsorship_supports_position: The bill text explicitly prohibits new landfills/junkyards within one mile of the river, with no exceptions for existing facilities or exemptions beyond on-site industrial operations. This suggests a **clear policy intent to restrict waste-related development near waterways.
evidence_quotes: Prohibit[s] the establishment of a new landfill or junk yard outside ... within one mile of the Chattahoochee River.
This section may be enforced by injunctive relief in the circuit court...
Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing in this section shall apply to any landfill or junk yard located on-site at an industrial facility.
review_reason: The bill’s intent is unambiguous: it restricts new waste facilities near a river. No additional context is required for analysis.
